'''Edward Marczewski''' (15 November 1907 – 17 October 1976<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pl.billiongraves.com/grave/Edward-Marczewski/30697465|title=pl.Billiongraves.com|accessdate=2019-04-22}}</ref>) was a Polish [[mathematician]]. He was born '''Szpilrajn''' but changed his name while hiding from Nazi persecution.<ref>Hartman, Stanislaw et al.: preface to "[http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Extras/Marczewski_papers.html Collected papers of Edward Marczewski]", Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences, Warsaw 1996.</ref>

Marczewski was a member of the [[Warsaw School (mathematics)|Warsaw School of Mathematics]]. His life and work after the [[World War II|Second World War]] were connected with [[Wrocław]], where he was among the creators of the Polish scientific centre. He worked at the [[Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences|State Institute of Mathematics]], which was incorporated into the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]] in 1952.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.impan.pl/en/insitute/about-us/history |title=History |website=impan.pl |access-date=7 December 2024 |archive-date=25 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241225182045/https://www.impan.pl/en/insitute/about-us/history |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Marczewski's main fields of interest were [[measure theory]], [[descriptive set theory]], [[general topology]], [[probability theory]] and [[universal algebra]]. He also published papers on real and complex analysis, applied mathematics and mathematical logic.

Marczewski proved that the [[topological dimension]], for arbitrary [[Metrisable space|metrisable]] [[separable space]] ''X'', coincides with the [[Hausdorff dimension]] under one of the metrics in ''X'' which induce the given topology of ''X'' (while otherwise the Hausdorff dimension is always greater or equal to the topological dimension).<ref>{{cite journal|author=Szpilrajn, E.|year=1937|title=La dimension et la mesure|journal=Fund. Math.|volume=28|pages=81–89|doi=10.4064/fm-28-1-81-89 |doi-access=free}}</ref> This is a fundamental theorem of [[fractal theory]]. (Certain contributions to this development were also made by [[Samuel Eilenberg]], see: [[Witold Hurewicz]] and [[Henry Wallman]], ''Dimension Theory'', 1941, Chapter VII.)
